scope: Authenticated actual lesson reader on isolated loopback synthetic fixture

reader_cases.title: Terms, partial sums and infinite series
reader_cases.instructions: Compare terms and partial sums using signed or fractional ratios. Change the term count and inspect convergent infinite sums and their remaining tails.

states.readout: Multiply by r = -0.75 each time. First term -4, term N = 0.00535142. Sum of the first 24 terms S_N = -2.28342. The infinite series converges to -2.28571. Signed remaining sum after N terms = -0.00229347. The terms themselves tend to 0.
Multiply by r = 1 each time. First term 4, term N = 4. Sum of the first 24 terms S_N = 96. The infinite series diverges: its partial sums have no finite limit. The terms themselves tend to 4.

Multiply by r = 0.25 each time. First term 1, term N = 1.4211e-14. Sum of the first 24 terms S_N = 1.33333. The infinite series converges to 1.33333. Signed remaining sum after N terms = 4.7370e-15. The terms themselves tend to 0.
Multiply by r = -4 each time. First term 0, term N = 0. Sum of the first 24 terms S_N = 0. The infinite series converges to 0. Signed remaining sum after N terms = 0. The terms themselves tend to 0.

reader_cases.title: Exponential growth, decay and logarithmic inverses
reader_cases.instructions: Compare growth and decay with fractional or negative exponents. Exchange graph coordinates to inspect the inverse, and see why base 1 has no logarithm.

states.readout: 0.5^(0.5) = approximately 0.707107. log base 0.5 of this value = 0.5. The points (0.5, 0.707107) and (0.707107, 0.5) exchange coordinates.
1^(-0.5) = approximately 1. Base 1 gives 1 for every exponent. An inverse cannot recover a unique exponent, so log base 1 is undefined.
5^(3) = 125. log base 5 of this value = 3. The points (3, 125) and (125, 3) exchange coordinates. The selected point pair is outside the displayed coordinate window; its values are still calculated.
